title: Stamp Act
summary: British Parliament imposed direct taxes on the colonies, sparking widespread protests and the rallying cry of 'no taxation without representation.'

title: Boston Massacre
summary: British soldiers killed five colonists during a confrontation, inflaming anti-British sentiment throughout the colonies.

title: Boston Tea Party
summary: Colonists dumped 342 chests of British tea into Boston Harbor to protest the Tea Act and taxation policies.

details.participants: American colonists, many disguised as Mohawk Indians, organized by the Sons of Liberty
details.target: Three British merchant ships: the Dartmouth, the Eleanor, and the Beaver
details.amount: 342 chests of tea, valued at approximately £9,000 (roughly $1.7 million in modern currency)
details.cause: Protest against the Tea Act of 1773, which granted the British East India Company a monopoly on tea sales in the colonies and maintained the principle of Parliament's right to tax the colonies
details.significance: The destruction of the tea galvanized colonial resistance, prompted Britain to pass the Coercive Acts (Intolerable Acts) in 1774, and accelerated the path toward revolution
details.outcome: No colonists were killed, but the British response hardened colonial resolve and united the colonies against British rule

title: Battles of Lexington and Concord
summary: The first military engagements of the Revolutionary War began when British troops attempted to seize colonial military supplies.

title: Declaration of Independence
summary: The Continental Congress formally declared the thirteen colonies independent from British rule on July 4th.

title: Battle of Yorktown
summary: American and French forces defeated the British army, effectively ending major combat operations and securing American independence.

title: Storming of the Bastille
summary: Parisians stormed the Bastille, a medieval fortress and symbol of royal tyranny, marking the beginning of the French Revolution.

details.significance: The fortress held only seven prisoners, but its capture became the defining moment of the French Revolution and galvanized revolutionary fervor
details.cause: King Louis XVI's dismissal of popular finance minister Jacques Necker and the threat of military force against the assembly
details.outcome: The fall of the Bastille demonstrated the power of popular uprising and the vulnerability of the old regime, inspiring revolutionary movements throughout Europe

title: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
summary: The National Constituent Assembly adopted a declaration proclaiming universal principles of human rights and popular sovereignty, influenced by the American Revolution.

title: Execution of King Louis XVI
summary: King Louis XVI was executed by guillotine on January 21, 1793, marking the radical phase of the French Revolution and the destruction of the ancien régime.
